description: A composite EBSD figure of eight panels from Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8C low-density steel multiaxially forged (MAF) for 0, 1, 3 and 5 passes. (a-d) are image quality (IQ) maps with grain boundaries superimposed; each carries a 60 µm scale bar and a legend headed "Boundaries: Rotation Angle" with columns Min / Max / Fraction, the green row 1°-15° and the red row 15°-180°. (a) MAF-0: coarse equiaxed grains, fractions 0.367 green and 0.622 red. (b) MAF-1: 0.708 green / 0.292 red, with a dense green low-angle subgrain network inside grains. (c) MAF-3: 0.759 green / 0.240 red. (d) MAF-5: 0.301 green / 0.699 red, a red-dominated banded, blocky substructure. (e-h) are inverse pole figure (IPF) maps of the normal / pressing direction for MAF-0, MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5 with the same 60 µm scale bars; (h) carries the IPF colour key triangle (111 apex, 001 and 101 base corners) that applies to (e-h). (e) shows a few large, uniformly coloured grains — strongly textured — whereas (f)-(h) show progressively more colour variation, grain fragmentation and dark low-IQ bands. The figure demonstrates that low-angle boundary fraction peaks after 3 passes while the texture is progressively randomised.

observations.observation: Panel (a) legend 'Boundaries: Rotation Angle' gives Fraction 0.367 for 1°-15° (green) and 0.622 for 15°-180° (red) in MAF-0.
Panel (b) legend gives Fraction 0.708 for 1°-15° and 0.292 for 15°-180° in MAF-1.
Panel (c) legend gives Fraction 0.759 for 1°-15° and 0.240 for 15°-180° in MAF-3.
Panel (d) legend gives Fraction 0.301 for 1°-15° and 0.699 for 15°-180° in MAF-5.
Panels (a-d) each contain a 60 µm scale bar and the IQ maps (a-d) and IPF maps (e-h) all share the same 60 µm scale bar.
Panel (h) contains the IPF colour key triangle whose corners are labelled 111 (top), 001 (bottom left) and 101 (bottom right).
The IPF map of MAF-0, panel (e), consists of a small number of large grains of nearly uniform colour, whereas (f)-(h) show many more distinct colours and fragmented, banded grains.
Green and red lines are superimposed on the IQ maps for boundaries having misorientation angles of 1°-15° and 15°-180°, respectively.
The caption states the IPF maps (e-h) are of the normal direction or pressing direction for MAF-0, MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5 respectively.
The citing text states MAF-0 has a high angle boundary fraction of 0.62, matching the red fraction 0.622 printed in panel (a).
The citing text states that after 1 pass (MAF-1) the high angle boundary fraction drops to 0.29 and the low angle boundary fraction rises to 0.70, matching the printed 0.292/0.708 in panel (b).
The citing text states the low angle boundary fraction increases rapidly up to 3 passes and reaches a maximum value of 0.75, matching the printed 0.759 in panel (c).
The citing text states that after 5 passes some low angle boundaries convert to high angle boundaries and the high angle fraction rises to 0.69, matching the printed 0.699 in panel (d).
The citing text states that in MAF-0 the [101] direction of a significant number of grains, and the [111] direction of another significant fraction, lie parallel to the pressing direction (panel e).
The citing text states that with increasing number of MAF passes the grains become randomised in orientation (panels f-h).

subfigures.description: IQ map of MAF-0 with coarse equiaxed grains, mostly red (high-angle) boundaries; 60 µm scale bar. Legend fractions: green 1°-15° = 0.367, red 15°-180° = 0.622.
IQ map of MAF-1 with a dense green (low-angle) boundary network inside grains; 60 µm scale bar. Legend fractions: 1°-15° = 0.708, 15°-180° = 0.292.
IQ map of MAF-3, heavily subdivided by green low-angle boundaries; 60 µm scale bar. Legend fractions: 1°-15° = 0.759, 15°-180° = 0.240.
IQ map of MAF-5, dominated by red high-angle boundaries forming a banded/blocky structure; 60 µm scale bar. Legend fractions: 1°-15° = 0.301, 15°-180° = 0.699.
IPF map (normal/pressing direction) of MAF-0: a few large grains each of nearly uniform colour (light green, blue, pink/red, lavender), indicating strong texture; 60 µm scale bar.
IPF map of MAF-1: many differently coloured, deformed and elongated grains (yellow, orange, cyan, blue, magenta), indicating the texture is being broken up; 60 µm scale bar.
IPF map of MAF-3: strongly fragmented, multi-colour (green, purple, blue, pink) banded grain structure; 60 µm scale bar.
IPF map of MAF-5: blocky, fragmented grains with many dark/black (poorly indexed) bands; includes the IPF colour key triangle labelled 111 (apex), 001 and 101 (base corners); 60 µm scale bar.

unreadable_items: The dark/black unindexed bands visible in panels (h) (and to a lesser extent d and g) are not identified or labelled in the figure
No colour-scale bar or step size is printed on the IPF maps; the colour key unit triangle appears only in panel (h) and is assumed to apply to (e)-(g)
